newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up, ACCESS holds after AGAs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up, ACCESS holds after AGAs.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures, helped by technical buying and talk of firmer cash, ended higher Wednesday in fairly active trade, then held relatively steady on ACCESS after weekly gas inventory data.
June gained 4.2 cents to close at $2.184 per million British thermal units, then on ACCESS traded around unchanged after the report. July settled 3.9 cents higher at $2.204.
"The AGAs were on the high side of expectations but no big deal. It looks like ACCESS is shrugging it off," said one East Coast trader, noting fund buying early in the day helped rally the complex.

AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 25 bcf, at the high side of expectations, and were now 213 bcf, or 33 percent, above year-ago levels. For the same week last year, overall inventories gained 68 bcf.
While storage remains well-above last year's record lows, some said current stock levels lagged the three-year average, raising the prospect for steady injection demand, at least early in the season.

In addition, traders said 6-10 day forecasts for hotter Texas and Southwest weather should support the early-May physical market though few expected much higher prices without a broader heat wave that included the Midwest and Northeast.

Technical traders said June's break this morning above resistance at $2.18 chould lead to a test of next resistance in the $2.24 area. Further selling should emerge ahead of the $2.385 contract high. But some said the market was overbought and due for a correction. June support was seen at $2.05 and then along the up trendline in the $2.01 area.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices notionally gained more than a nickel Wednesday to the $2.10-15 range. Midcon pipes were up a few cents to the mid-to-high $1.90s. New York city gate gas also was modestly higher at about $2.40.
The NYMEX 12-month Hub strip rose 3.1 cents to $2.262. NYMEX said 47,164 Hub contracts traded, up from Tuesday's revised tally of 31,556.

On the KCBT, June finished 3.7 cents higher at $2.017, while deferreds ended up by 3.5 to four cents. The East/West spread widened by one-half cent to 16.7 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 368 lots changed hands, down from Tuesday's total of 465.
